name: rawStreamOpen
description: Open a provider-scoped raw byte stream: one HTTP request (body sent whole) to the configured provider's domain, the response pulled with rawStreamRead. The host never parses the body, so any wire format works (OpenAI / Anthropic / Responses JSON+SSE, Connect/protobuf, ...). Secrets reach the request only through `{{secret:NAME}}` placeholders in header and query-parameter values, substituted host-side; NAME `api_key` is the provider's API key, any other NAME an entry of the provider config's `secrets`. Redirects are followed, but a hop that leaves the provider's domain drops every header a secret was substituted into. With `captureSecrets` the response is buffered (<= 1 MB), the named JSON fields are stored as provider secrets, and the guest receives the body with them redacted. Resolves with the response head; `streamId` in the result echoes the caller's id, or the one the host minted. Additive action: a host without it answers unknown-action, and the guest treats the provider as unavailable. Values may also carry `{{oauth:access_token}}` / `{{oauth:account_id}}` for an OAuth-backed provider: the host runs its token refresh / exchange first (NexusOAuthManager::EnsureFreshToken) and substitutes them under the same domain anchor; OAUTH_UNAVAILABLE when not signed in. Manifest primitive model.rawStreamOpen.oauth. A value that carried only an empty `{{oauth:account_id}}` (a sign-in with no account id) is omitted rather than sent empty — manifest primitive model.rawStreamOpen.oauthOptional.

inputs.name: providerId
inputs.description: Configured provider whose secrets may be referenced and whose active base URL bounds the target: `url` must share its scheme and registrable domain.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: Absolute request URL. Must not contain secrets — put them in `queryParams`.

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Request headers, string -> string, values may contain `{{secret:NAME}}`; one with no usable value refuses the open with SECRET_UNAVAILABLE and `error.data` = {secret, reason}, reason `missing` (nothing stored), `unreadable` (stored sealed, but this OS keystore will not open it; enter it again) or `keystore_not_ready` (a later open can succeed) — a malformed placeholder, or an older host, sends no data. User-Agent and auth headers are the caller's; Cookie, Host, Content-Length and Proxy-Authorization are rejected (INVALID_ARGS). Without a User-Agent the provider's preset (if any) is sent.

inputs.name: queryParams
inputs.description: Query parameters appended (URL-encoded) after the domain check, string -> string, values may contain `{{secret:NAME}}` (e.g. `key` for Google).

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Request body bytes, sent whole; empty for none. Content-Type comes from `headers` (default application/octet-stream).

inputs.name: captureSecrets
inputs.description: [{pointer, secret}]: RFC 6901 JSON pointers into the response body whose string values are stored (sealed) as the provider secret `secret` (not `api_key`) and replaced by "[captured]" in the body the guest receives. The final read carries `captured: {secret: sealedValue}` for the guest to persist in settings.json. A 2xx body that is not JSON is withheld (CAPTURE_FAILED).

inputs.name: streamId
inputs.description: Caller-chosen id, 8-64 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. The host keys the stream by it, so `rawStreamCancel` can cancel the request before the response head; the pending open then fails with `CANCELLED`. Refused with `INVALID_ARGS` if malformed or already open. Omitted: the host mints one. An older host ignores it and answers with its own id.

inputs.name: idleTimeoutMs
inputs.description: Abort when no response bytes arrive for this long. Default 90000. Keep it at or below 90000: the guest transport's `model` route fallback is 100 s, so a longer native wait on the response head would be cut off guest-side first.

inputs.name: maxResponseBytes
inputs.description: Abort once the response body exceeds this. Default 200000000; capped at 1048576 with captureSecrets.
